fact: 1907年10月16日，投机商F. Augustus Heinze与Charles W. Morse试图轧空在纽约场外市场（curb）交易的铜矿公司United Copper股票失败，其失败暴露出银行、经纪行与信托公司之间互联的董事网络，构成当年10月金融恐慌的直接导火索。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907 (Jon R. Moen & Ellis W. Tallman)
sources.quote: On October 16, 1907, two minor speculators, F. Augustus Heinze and Charles W. Morse, suffered huge losses in a failed attempt to corner the stock of United Copper, a copper mining company traded on the curb.

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: Such a shock occurred on October 16, 1907, when F. Augustus Heinze's scheme to corner the stock of United Copper Company failed. Although United Copper was only a moderately important firm, the collapse of Heinze's scheme, exposed an intricate network of interlocking directorates across banks, brokerage houses, and trust companies in New York City.

fact: 10月18日（周五）传出国民商业银行总裁Charles T. Barney与Morse的关联后，纽约第三大信托公司Knickerbocker Trust遭遇挤兑；国民商业银行10月21日宣布不再为其清算支票，10月22日Knickerbocker在约三小时挤兑、付出近800万美元现金后于中午前后停业，成为全面恐慌的标志。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907 (Jon R. Moen & Ellis W. Tallman)
sources.quote: On Friday, October 18, news broke that the president of Knickerbocker Trust, Charles T. Barney, was an associate of Morse. The news sparked a run on Knickerbocker. ... The next day, after depositors had withdrawn nearly $8 million, it suspended operations.

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: Late that Monday afternoon the National Bank of Commerce announced that it would stop clearing checks for the Knickerbocker Trust Company, the third largest trust in New York City. ... On October 22 Knickerbocker underwent a run for three hours before suspending operations just after noon, having paid out $8 million in cash.

fact: 1907年成为埃利斯岛入境审查史上最繁忙的一年，当年经该站处理的移民超过一百万人，纽约的同乡聚居与劳动力供给网络在恐慌年份仍持续扩张。

sources.title: Statue of Liberty–Ellis Island Foundation — Ellis Island Overview History
sources.quote: In fact, 1907 marked the busiest year at Ellis Island with over one million immigrants processed.

fact: 1907年10月22日Knickerbocker停业当日，纽约证券交易所隔夜拆放利率（call money）年化水平从前一日的9.5%跃升至70%，两日后达100%；10月24日开盘利率6%，一度出现60%的报价而无人放款，当日最后记录成交回到开盘水平，反映现金几乎枯竭。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907 (Jon R. Moen & Ellis W. Tallman)
sources.quote: On the day Knickerbocker closed, October 22, the annualized rate jumped from 9.5 percent to 70 percent, then to 100 percent two days later. At times, there were no credit offers at that rate.

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: The opening rate for call money was 6 percent, but exchange president Ransom H. Thomas noticed a serious scarcity of money. At one point that morning a bid of 60 percent went out for call money. Yet, even at that exorbitant rate, no money was offered. ... While Thomas traveled to Morgan's office, the call money rate on the exchange reached 100 percent.

fact: 10月26日（周六）纽约清算所委员会设立小组发行清算所贷款证（clearing-house loan certificates）：首批发行后贷款即时增加约1100万美元，其后三周内纽约市发行超过1.1亿美元；据A. Piatt Andrew统计，整个恐慌期间全国流通的代币性质替代现金接近5亿美元。贷款证只能在银行间流通，构成联储出现前的临时流动性机制。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907 (Jon R. Moen & Ellis W. Tallman)
sources.quote: After an unusual delay of five days, the New York Clearing House Committee met on Saturday, October 26, and formed a panel to facilitate the issuance of clearing-house loan certificates. These were the predecessor to discount window loans from the Federal Reserve System and provided a temporary increase in liquidity.

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: Following the first issue of clearinghouse loan certificates on October 26 during the 1907 Panic, loans initially increased by about $11 million. During the next three weeks more than $110 million in certificates were issued in New York City. Over the entire course of the Panic, nearly $500 million in currency substitutes circulated throughout the country as a 'principal means of payment,' according to Andrew (1910, 515).

sources.title: William C. Van Antwerp, The Stock Exchange from Within (New York: Doubleday, Page & Co., 1913), Chapter VI, Project Gutenberg eBook #60082
sources.quote: Clearing-house certificates were resorted to at practically all banking centres throughout the country; there was a general requirement of time notices for withdrawal of savings bank deposits

fact: 财政部长George B. Cortelyou于10月23日晚与纽约主要金融家会晤后，10月24日上午将2500万美元财政部资金存入国民银行；10月21日至31日期间财政部合计存入3760万美元并提供3600万美元小面额钞票应对挤兑，至11月中旬财政部可用营运资金降至约500万美元。

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: Secretary of the Treasury George Cortelyou and the major New York financiers met on the evening of Wednesday, October 23, and discussed plans to combat the crisis. Cortelyou deposited $25 million of the Treasury's funds in national banks the following morning. Between October 21 and October 31, the Treasury deposited a total of $37.6 million in New York national banks and provided $36 million in small bills to meet runs.

fact: 1906年纽约州立法要求信托公司按存款15%提留准备金，但其中仅5%须以库存现金形式持有；同期纽约中央储备城市国民银行须保持25%的金银或法偿准备。信托公司现金准备薄弱（约为存款的5%）且大量资金用于对股票市场经纪人的无抵押日间贷款，是1907年挤兑集中于信托公司的制度根源。

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: In 1906 New York State instituted a requirement that trusts maintain reserves at 15 percent of deposits, but only 5 percent of deposits needed to be kept as currency in the vault. ... National banks in central reserve cities like New York were required to keep a 25 percent reserve in the form of specie or legal tender

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907 (Jon R. Moen & Ellis W. Tallman)
sources.quote: As a result, they held a low percentage of cash reserves relative to deposits, around 5 percent, compared with 25 percent for national banks.

fact: 纽约第二大信托公司Trust Company of America在两周挤兑中付出约4750万美元存款；10月23日晨前Benjamin Strong完成资产评估后，J.P. Morgan在收盘前向其调拨约300万美元，使其次日得以恢复营业；J.D. Rockefeller同期向Union Trust存入1000万美元以支持信托体系。

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: During the span of the run, which lasted two weeks, Trust Company of America reportedly paid out $47.5 million in deposits. ... Morgan channeled about $3 million to Trust Company just before closing time, which allowed it to resume business the next day. ... J.D. Rockefeller deposited $10 million with the Union Trust to help the trusts and announced his support for Morgan.

fact: 恐慌期间，J.P. Morgan与国民城市银行总裁James Stillman、第一国民银行总裁George Baker组成非正式救市核心；Morgan请Banker's Trust副总裁Benjamin Strong（后任纽约联储首任行长）清查Knickerbocker账目，因时间不足无法判定偿付能力，Morgan拒绝援助该信托；10月25日摩根集团组织1000万美元、第一国民银行200万美元、Kuhn Loeb 50万美元的资金池；11月4日促成信托公司总裁们组成的2500万美元联合贷款。Morgan还向证交所贷款柱直接输送现金，使交易所维持开业。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907 (Jon R. Moen & Ellis W. Tallman)
sources.quote: The New York Stock Exchange remained open largely because of the legendary actions of Morgan, who solicited cash from large financial and industrial institutions and then had it delivered directly to the loan post at the exchange to support brokers who were willing to extend credit.

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: On October 25 another money pool was required. About $10 million came from the Morgan group, $2 million from First National, and $500,000 from Kuhn, Loeb, and Company. ... The funds were provided on November 4 after several nights of negotiation.

fact: 停业后的Knickerbocker Trust于1908年3月在注入240万美元新资本后复业；同期全国少数地区的贷款证等现金替代物迟至1908年3月仍在流通，显示恐慌清算延续至次年春季。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907 (Jon R. Moen & Ellis W. Tallman)
sources.quote: By closing temporarily, Knickerbocker prevented depositors from gaining any further access to their deposits; it reopened in March 1908 following the infusion of $2.4 million in new capital.

sources.title: EH.net Encyclopedia — The Panic of 1907 (Jon Moen, University of Mississippi)
sources.quote: Although convertibility was widely restored by the beginning of January, in a few instances loan certificates and other substitutes for cash circulated as late as March 1908.

fact: 1907年恐慌造成显著实体收缩：1908年工业产出下降17%，实际GNP下降12%，严重程度仅次于大萧条；但实体部门在约一年多后快速复苏。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — The Panic of 1907 (Jon R. Moen & Ellis W. Tallman)
sources.quote: It is also important to note that the Panic of 1907 had severe real effects. Industrial output fell 17 percent in 1908, and real GNP fell by 12 percent. Only the Great Depression was more severe. But unlike the Great Depression or the recent Great Recession, the real sector recovered rapidly, in little over a year after 1907.

fact: 1907年，纽约投资银行家J.P. Morgan收购田纳西煤铁铁路公司（TCI）控制权，将伯明翰的钢铁产能并入其刚组建不久的美国钢铁公司体系；美国钢铁日后以“匹兹堡加价”（Pittsburgh Plus）定价公式抑制TCI与匹兹堡竞争。该交易以私人谈判方式完成。

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Alabama — Birmingham Iron and Steel Companies
sources.quote: In 1907, New York investment banker J. P. Morgan, who had recently created the world's largest company, United States Steel Corporation, acquired control of TCI. Local supporters of the purchase initially believed that this development would guarantee Birmingham's future greatness, but their expectations were wrong. U.S. Steel officials did not want TCI to compete with Pittsburgh and other steelmaking centers and imposed a discriminatory pricing formula, known as "Pittsburgh Plus"

fact: 认识到国家不能继续依赖个别富豪稳定金融，国会于1908年5月30日通过《奥尔德里奇-弗里兰法案》（Aldrich-Vreeland Act）：授权紧急货币发行，并设立由参议员Nelson Aldrich主持的18人全国货币委员会研究货币银行制度改革，成为1913年《联邦储备法》的直接立法前奏。

sources.title: Federal Reserve History — Federal Reserve Act Signed into Law (Staff of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City)
sources.quote: Recognizing that the nation could not continue to rely on wealthy individuals to stem an economic and financial crisis, Congress passed the Aldrich-Vreeland Act on May 30, 1908. The legislation provided for the issuance of emergency currency and created the eighteen-member National Monetary Commission, chaired by Sen. Nelson Aldrich, to determine what changes were necessary to the nation's monetary system and laws related to banking and currency.

fact: 恐慌后舆论矛头指向华尔街，纽约州州长Charles Evans Hughes为防止仓促立法，于1909年任命委员会调查纽约证券交易所；该委员会历经半年调查后认为保证金交易本身合法，主张改革应由交易所内部自律完成，而非立法禁止。

sources.title: William C. Van Antwerp, The Stock Exchange from Within (New York: Doubleday, Page & Co., 1913), Chapter VI, Project Gutenberg eBook #60082
sources.quote: Thus it happened that Governor Hughes of New York, doubtless moved to forestall hasty law-making, appointed a committee to investigate the Stock Exchange. ... 'Purchasing securities on margin is as legitimate a transaction as the purchase of any property in which part payment is deferred. We, therefore, see no reason whatsoever for recommending the radical change suggested that margin trading be prohibited.'

fact: 1907年12月23日，美国战争部发布第486号规格书（Specification No. 486）招标“重于空气的飞行机器”，要求载两人飞行125英里、时速不低于40英里、滞空1小时；莱特兄弟于1908年1月27日以25000美元投标，显示军用航空采购在恐慌年份仍未中断。

sources.title: U.S. Centennial of Flight — Wright Brothers: 1907-08 (FAA/Smithsonian-hosted essay)
sources.quote: On December 23, 1907, the U.S. War Department issued Specification No. 486 for a "Heavier-than-air Flying Machine." It stated that the aircraft must be able to carry two men for a distance of 125 miles (201 kilometers) at a minimum speed of 40 miles per hour (64 kilometers per hour). It must be able to stay aloft for one hour between refuelings... On January 27, 1908, the Wrights submitted their formal bid to the War Department for one aircraft that would cost $25,000.

fact: 作为1907年纽约城市交通背景：纽约第一条地铁——Interborough Rapid Transit（IRT）线于1904年10月27日开通运营，至1907年仍是全市唯一的地下快速交通系统，支撑曼哈顿向北扩展与外围地价重构。

sources.title: nycsubway.org — The First Subway
sources.quote: On October 27, 1904, the first IRT subway line opened, and the city would never be the same. City Hall station, pictured above, was the showpiece of the new subway.

fact: 全国工资参照：据MeasuringWorth（Officer & Williamson）年度序列，1907年美国制造业生产工人平均小时报酬（含福利）为0.17美元，1908年降至0.16美元；非熟练工货币工资指数为172.0（1860=100），1908年降至164.0、1909年166.0。即恐慌后的1908年名义工资水平回落约2%—5%，与纽约建筑业工会工资率的水平对照见1907-US-COST-001。该序列的原始文献为David & Solar（1977）与Margo（2000）。

fact: 美国物价水平与消费篮子：MeasuringWorth年度CPI（1982-84=100，对BLS CPI-U向前延伸）1907年为9.11，1908年降至8.92、1909年8.82——恐慌后一年物价下降约2.1%、两年累计约3.2%，持现金者的购买力在1908—09年上升；同站消费篮子序列估计1907年美国消费单位年均支出972美元（1908年945美元），消费单位平均3.40人。消费篮子为对早期年份的历史估计值（BLS入户调查始于1913年后），用作量级参照而非精确官价。
